The {place} is boarded up. Come back another day.

Pushing open the creaky shop door...
The shop bell jingles...
"Welcome, welcome! Mind the cat."
"Potions, tonics, a bit of everything!"
"Gold first, questions later."
"Come back alive, now!"
"Safe travels, hero."
The smith sets the {gem} into your {weapon}.
Sparks fly. The {gem} now glows in your {weapon}.
The smith wipes soot from her brow. "Gems, sockets or steel?"
Heat rolls off the forge. "Bring me something worth fixing."
"None of what you carry can hold a gem. Buy something proper."
"You've no gems to set. Come back when the dungeon pays out."
"Coin first, hero."
"That's not enough gold, and I don't do favours."

The {gem} cracks as it leaves your {item}. Nothing left but dust.

"Racks are empty. Come back another day."
"The {item} would crush you. Come back at level {level}."
"Your pack's full. Sell something first."

Nothing here but crumbs and lint.

A small red vial that smells of cherries and iron. Closes wounds in moments.
Fizzy and bitter. For a few heartbeats the world seems to slow down around you.
A grey, chalky brew. Your skin stiffens like boiled leather.
Heavy, cold and green with age. It must open something below the village.
A shard of black iron that still feels warm. Whispers when you aren't listening.
A roll of thin picks and tension bars. Every rogue's oldest friend.
A blacksmith's hammer made for heads instead of horseshoes. Slow, but it lands hard.
Light and wickedly sharp. Rewards a steady hand with deadly strikes.
So thin it barely makes a sound leaving its sheath.
Yew wood and waxed string. Fells a stag at a hundred paces.
Knotted oak carved with old runes. Crackles faintly when you grip it.
A blade that never quite stops smouldering. The Bone Lich kept it close.
Its edge drinks the life of whatever it cuts. Wild, hungry and never the same twice.
A chip of the drake's fire, still glowing. Sets a weapon burning.
Cold enough to sting your fingers. Frost gathers on anything it touches.
Tiny lightning flickers inside it, like a storm in a bottle.
Dark red and faintly warm, like a heartbeat. Hungers for life.
A pale blue crystal humming with stored magic.
At midnight, the bell rang beneath Hollowmere. By morning, Wren's chair was empty.
Her mother remembered having a daughter. She could not remember her name.
The elders opened the dungeon gate. Bring back the bell's clapper, they said.
From far below, the bell rang again.
The Crypt Warden raises its rusted keys. The bell is not a weapon; it warns the dead to stay below.
A name is scratched into the Warden's key ring. You recognize the handwriting from Hollowmere.
Vexara coils around the clapper. The elders broke the pact, she snarls. Now the seal is failing.
The drake's flames gutter as she speaks: the King has kept something beneath the mountain asleep.
Malgrath's skull turns toward you. The bell takes names so the thing below cannot learn them.
The Lich points to the surface. Your elders knew the price. They chose to break the pact anyway.
The Dread King lowers his blade. I chose who the village forgot. I have hated every toll.
I can no longer keep the seal. Take my crown, take my burden, or break the bell and face what wakes.
You smash the bell. Its last note shakes dust from every tomb. Beneath the dungeon, something opens its eyes.
The bell breaks. No more names will be taken. Far below, the ancient hunger stirs.
You ring the bell once more. Hollowmere is safe tonight. The village forgets another name.
The seal holds. The price is paid again, and the bell waits for the next midnight.
You speak your own name into the bell. The seal closes. Hollowmere remembers everyone but you.
The bell rings with your name. The village is safe, and no one remembers the hero who saved it.
